outcome: Difficulty of vacuum extraction (defined by number of vacuum pulls: easy group <=3 pulls, difficult/impossible group >=4 pulls)
cohort: The study included 72 primiparous women with singleton pregnancies at full dilatation and >=37-weeks gestation who underwent transperineal ultrasound before vacuum placement for fetal extraction.
finding: Intrapartum transperineal ultrasound parameters, specifically progression angle, fetal head direction, and midline angle, are strong predictors of the difficulty of vacuum extraction.
mod_finding: The study identified specific intrapartum transperineal ultrasound parameters that can predict the difficulty of vacuum-assisted delivery.
birth_weight: Newborn weight (3147 g in the easy group versus 3540 g in the difficult group)
